text:
Issue 87. Five links this week, and three of them deserve more than a quick click.

Every week we go through new releases, updates, and side projects so you don't have to. Here's what made the cut.

**A new Rust linter.** It's stricter than most setups, and when it flags something, it explains why in plain terms. The goal is to catch subtle mistakes early without flooding you with warnings that don't matter.

**A Git GUI.** Plenty of you live in the terminal, and so do we. But sometimes it's just faster to see your branches, diffs, and history laid out on screen. This one is built to be quick, with a clean layout.

**A tracing tool.** If you've ever stared at a slow request and wondered where the time went, try this. It follows execution across your whole system, so you can find the bottleneck without guessing.

The last two links are smaller finds that we liked.

If you just signed up, welcome. There are 9,400 of you now. On to the links.
